# 18 Draw generics with angle brackets, as Mermaid does

## Outcome

`class Square~Shape~` draws as `Square<Shape>` and a member typed `+List~int~ items` draws as
`+List<int> items` — the tilde is Mermaid's *authoring* delimiter, not its rendered one, and this
board's whole premise is parity with what Mermaid draws.

## Why this ticket exists

Ticket 09 composed the class-name text and asked the board to settle the spelling before ticket 10
or 17 assert on rendered text. It kept the author's tildes, reasoning that a name drawn as
`List<int>` beside a member type drawn as `List~int~` would be inconsistent — which is correct as
far as it goes, and is exactly why the fix has to cover both: the two must agree, and Mermaid
converts both.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A class whose model carries a generic composes its name as `Id<Generic>`; a class with no
  generic is unchanged.
- [ ] A member whose type or return type contains `~T~` composes with `<T>`; a member with no
  tildes is unchanged, and a tilde used as a **visibility marker** (`~packagePrivate`) is
  untouched — that is a different token in the same character.
- [ ] Nested generics convert throughout: `Map~String, List~int~~` draws as
  `Map<String, List<int>>`.
- [ ] The class box is measured from the converted text, so a name or member whose rendering grew
  or shrank still fits its frame.
- [ ] An unbalanced tilde in author input does not corrupt the rest of the line — decide what it
  draws, document it, and test it.
- [ ] Ticket 04's and 09's existing tests still pass; where one asserted the tilde spelling,
  update the expectation rather than weakening the assertion.

Two things round 3's standards review flagged in this same file, which you own and should close
while you are in here:

- [ ] **`buildClassModel` composes its own copy of the member line text**, as the union key for
  merging repeat declarations, duplicating `memberText` here. Once this ticket changes the drawn
  spelling, the two legitimately diverge: the model keys on `List~int~`, the layout draws
  `List<int>`. That is *fine* — a union key only has to be internally consistent — but the
  duplicated function's comment currently claims layout's spelling is authoritative, which will
  become false. Either make the divergence explicit in both comments, or (the reviewer's
  suggestion, and the better shape) compose the line once in the model and carry it on the
  contract so layout draws what the model already decided. The second option touches
  `contracts.ts` and `buildClassModel.ts` — out of your write scope — so if you prefer it, say so
  and stop rather than reaching for those files.
- [ ] **`placedById` and `boxById` hold the same nodes in different coordinate spaces** (pre- and
  post-translation), told apart only by name. One future `placedById.get(...)` outside the frame
  code silently misplaces whatever reads it. Rename both to say which space they are in.
- [ ] **The translation may be dead code.** Round 3's reviewer could not drive a namespace frame
  past the origin in either axis, with short or tall labels — the shift was always zero. Try to
  reach it yourself. If you can, leave it and add the test that reaches it. If you cannot, delete
  it: untested defensive geometry that maintains two coordinate spaces is exactly the hazard the
  rename above is working around, and the two problems cancel if the shift goes.

Exact places the tilde spelling is asserted today, so nothing is missed (from round 3's review):
`layoutClassDiagram.ts` `classNameText` (whose doc comment argues *for* tildes and must be
rewritten) and `memberText`; `layoutClassDiagram.test.ts:426,429`;
`renderClassDiagramToSVG.test.ts:229,232`. Must **not** change: `index.test.ts:178,1135` and
`examples/class-core.srn:6` assert `~String tag`, where the tilde is a package-visibility marker,
not a generic — a different token that happens to share the character.

## Test seam

`layoutClassDiagram(model, options): PositionedClassDiagram` — unit level, deterministic fake
measurer. The composition lives in layout because layout is what measures the text; the renderer
draws whatever string it is handed.
